title: Fixed-retention GLV rho v12: measured selected law and itemized costs (qualification HOLD)

claims.statement: Conditional analytic full-production secp256k1 ECDLP claim: the specified fixed-spacing, capped-retention GLV class-rho algorithm recovers a uniform challenge logarithm with probability at least 0.40 within 2^(3267/25) classical target-operation equivalents at protected C=1000. Let N=(r-1)/6, nu=137/100, T=ceil(sqrt((98859/100000)*nu^2*N)), L=40*2^64, K=T+1024*L, M=2^72 records and S=2^85 event/start caps. H-Rom lower-bounds the useful-core collision probability by P0=1-exp(-(7/10)*T*(T-1)/(2*N)). H-window explicitly requires conditional completion of the collision-selected pair with efficiency eta=8521/10000, the downward finite selected-law envelope, plus the separately stated spatial and cap-loss bounds; it is not a uniform-pair birthday deduction. H-rate bounds both emitted endpoint and all-terminal first moments by (11/10)*K/2^64. Failure precedes pool overflow, and no record is evicted, replaced or filtered. Success arithmetic is eta*P0 minus all listed debits. Itemized scalar64 costs sum2432 instructions per tick below an8000 ceiling; the entire ceiling and all nonreference work receive6/5 repricing and complete work receives27/25 reserve. Full starting scalars and two-limb lengths occupy192-byte records; total peak is3*2^78+2^30 bytes, below2^80, with zero nonuniform advice. All preprocessing, failed trials, replay and verification are included. This is conditional analysis, not an unconditional theorem or production execution. Finite selected-law and terminal-path observations do not prove production rare-event magnitudes; production qualification remains explicitly on HOLD.
